question:
Find the part of the sentence that contains an error.

 

The new policy guidelines was announced by the HR department (a)/ during the quarterly meeting (b)/ to ensure compliance across all branches (c)/ before the fiscal year begins. (d)
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. (a).

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The plural subject "guidelines" requires the plural passive auxiliary "were announced", not the singular "was announced".

◦ Corrected sentence: The new policy guidelines were announced by the HR department during the quarterly meeting to ensure compliance across all branches before the fiscal year begins.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Part (b) is correct — "during the quarterly meeting" is a proper adverbial phrase.

 

• Part (c) is correct — "to ensure compliance across all branches" is a proper purpose phrase.

 

• Part (d) is correct — "before the fiscal year begins" correctly completes the sentence.

 

NOTE

 

• The safety instructions was issued by the supervisor. → were issued (passive verb must agree in number with the plural subject).

question:

The bridge was constructed by the engineers (a)/ and it were inaugurated by the minister (b)/ during a special ceremony last week. (c)/ No error (d)
solution_text:

Additional Information

question:
Find the part of the sentence that contains an error.

 

Several new regulations have been introduced by the government (a)/ to curb pollution levels in metropolitan cities, (b)/ and a dedicated task force have been formed (c)/ to monitor their implementation. (d)
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. (c).

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The singular collective subject "a dedicated task force" requires the singular auxiliary "has been formed", not "have been formed".

◦ Corrected sentence: Several new regulations have been introduced by the government to curb pollution levels in metropolitan cities, and a dedicated task force has been formed to monitor their implementation.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Part (a) is correct — "Several new regulations have been introduced by the government" is a correctly formed present perfect passive.

 

• Part (b) is correct — "to curb pollution levels in metropolitan cities," is a proper purpose phrase.

 

• Part (d) is correct — "to monitor their implementation" correctly completes the sentence.

 

NOTE

 

• A new committee have been set up to investigate the matter. → has been set up (singular collective noun + present perfect passive → singular auxiliary "has been").

question:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

 

According to the safety manual, a helmet ___ by every worker before entering the construction site.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. must be worn.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• With the modal "must", the passive form is "must be + past participle": "must be worn".

◦ Complete sentence: According to the safety manual, a helmet must be worn by every worker before entering the construction site.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1: "must wear" — this is the active form; the passive auxiliary "be" and past participle are missing.

 

• Option 2: "must wore" — this is an ungrammatical combination of a modal with the past tense form.

 

• Option 3: "must be wearing" — the continuous form is wrongly used instead of the simple modal passive "must be worn".

 

NOTE

 

• The safety gate must close before the machine starts. → must be closed before the machine starts (modal "must" + base verb → "must be" + past participle).

question:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

 

By the time the auditors arrived, all the financial records ___ digitally to prevent any loss.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. had been backed up.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The time marker "by the time the auditors arrived" signals an action completed before another past action, requiring the past perfect passive: "had been backed up".

◦ Complete sentence: By the time the auditors arrived, all the financial records had been backed up digitally to prevent any loss.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1: "have been backed up" — the present perfect is wrongly used instead of the past perfect "had been backed up".

 

• Option 2: "were backed up" — the simple past drops the sense of an action completed earlier than another past action.

 

• Option 4: "has been backed up" — the present perfect singular form is wrongly used, and it also fails to agree with the plural subject "all the financial records".

 

NOTE

 

• By the time the guests arrived, the hall had been decorated beautifully. (an action completed before another past action → past perfect passive).

question:
Find the part of the sentence that contains an error.

 

Despite repeated reminders from the regional offices, (a)/ delays in data collection continued unabated, (b)/ and as a result, the final proposal, which was due on Friday, (c)/ should have submitted much earlier by the committee. (d)
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. (d).

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The modal perfect passive requires "should have been + past participle": "should have been submitted", not "should have submitted".

◦ Corrected sentence: Despite repeated reminders from the regional offices, delays in data collection continued unabated, and as a result, the final proposal, which was due on Friday, should have been submitted much earlier by the committee.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Part (a) is correct — "Despite repeated reminders from the regional offices," is a proper concessive phrase.

 

• Part (b) is correct — "delays in data collection continued unabated," correctly describes the situation.

 

• Part (c) is correct — "and as a result, the final proposal, which was due on Friday," correctly leads into the main clause.

 

NOTE

 

• The report should have finished by the team before the review. → should have been finished (modal perfect passive requires "should have been" + past participle).

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

• Part (c) is correct — "and photography is strictly prohibited inside the main exhibition hall" is a correctly formed simple present passive.

 

• Option (d) No error — this is incorrect since an error exists in part (a).

 

NOTE

question:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

 

It ___ that regular exercise improves overall health and longevity.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. is generally believed.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• With a generic/indefinite agent, the passive typically drops the "by" phrase; the correct present-tense passive is simply "is generally believed".

◦ Complete sentence: It is generally believed that regular exercise improves overall health and longevity.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1: "is generally believe by people" — the base form "believe" is wrongly used instead of the past participle "believed"; besides, retaining "by people" here is unnecessary since the agent is vague and generic.

 

• Option 2: "is generally believing" — this is an ungrammatical active-like continuous form; the passive requires "is believed".

 

• Option 4: "was generally believed" — the past tense is wrongly used instead of the simple present "is believed", which suits a general, ongoing belief.

 

NOTE

 

• It is widely accepted that honesty is the best policy. (generic agent dropped in an impersonal passive statement of general truth).

question:
Find the part of the sentence that contains an error.

 

According to eyewitnesses, (a)/ a truck skidded off the wet road near the railway crossing late last night, (b)/ injuring two passersby, (c)/ and a serious accident was happened as a result of the driver's negligence. (d)
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. (d).

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The verb "happen" is intransitive and therefore has no passive form; the correct simple past form is "happened", not "was happened".

◦ Corrected sentence: According to eyewitnesses, a truck skidded off the wet road near the railway crossing late last night, injuring two passersby, and a serious accident happened as a result of the driver's negligence.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Part (a) is correct — "According to eyewitnesses," is a proper introductory phrase.

 

• Part (b) is correct — "a truck skidded off the wet road near the railway crossing late last night," is a correctly formed simple past active sentence.

 

• Part (c) is correct — "injuring two passersby," correctly describes the consequence.

 

NOTE

 

• The mistake was occurred due to a technical glitch. → the mistake occurred (intransitive verbs such as "occur", "happen", "arise" have no passive form).

question:
Find the part of the sentence that contains an error. If the sentence is free from error, select 'No error'.

 

A detailed report was given the manager by the analyst (a)/ and a copy was sent to the board of directors (b)/ for their review before the meeting. (c)/ No error (d)
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. (a).

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• When the direct object becomes the subject of the passive with a double-object verb like "give", the indirect object must be preceded by "to": "was given to the manager", not "was given the manager".

◦ Corrected sentence: A detailed report was given to the manager by the analyst and a copy was sent to the board of directors for their review before the meeting.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Part (b) is correct — "and a copy was sent to the board of directors" is a correctly formed passive with "to".

 

• Part (c) is correct — "for their review before the meeting" correctly completes the sentence.

 

• Option (d) No error — this is incorrect since an error exists in part (a).

 

NOTE

 

• A prize was awarded the winner by the chief guest. → was awarded to the winner (direct object as passive subject requires "to" before the indirect object).

question:

◦ Corrected sentence: During the night shift, the security guard was seen entering the restricted server room without proper authorisation, triggering an immediate internal investigation.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

question:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

 

On their first day last week, the new recruits ___ by the senior manager to complete the orientation module within a week.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. were instructed.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• With a verb followed by an object and a to-infinitive ("instructed...to complete"), the passive form is "were instructed...to complete", keeping the to-infinitive intact and matching the past tense of the context.

◦ Complete sentence: On their first day last week, the new recruits were instructed by the senior manager to complete the orientation module within a week.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1: "instructed" — this is the active form; the passive auxiliary "were" is missing.

 

• Option 2: "were instructing" — the active continuous form cannot combine with "by the senior manager" in this way; the correct passive form is "were instructed".

 

• Option 4: "are instructed" — the present tense is wrongly used instead of the simple past "were instructed".

 

NOTE

 

• The trainees were told by the coach to report early. (verb + object + to-infinitive, retained in the passive).

question:
Find the part of the sentence that contains an error.

 

Although some historians believe that the actual construction period remains uncertain, (a)/ it is said that the ancient fort was built by a local king several centuries ago, (b)/ and it has since become a major tourist attraction, (c)/ so it are widely regarded as a symbol of regional heritage. (d)
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. (d).

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The singular subject "it" requires the singular passive auxiliary "is widely regarded", not the plural "are widely regarded".

◦ Corrected sentence: Although some historians believe that the actual construction period remains uncertain, it is said that the ancient fort was built by a local king several centuries ago, and it has since become a major tourist attraction, so it is widely regarded as a symbol of regional heritage.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Part (a) is correct — "Although some historians believe that the actual construction period remains uncertain," is a proper concessive clause.

 

• Part (b) is correct — "it is said that the ancient fort was built by a local king several centuries ago," is a correctly formed impersonal passive.

 

• Part (c) is correct — "and it has since become a major tourist attraction," is a correctly formed present perfect.

 

NOTE

 

• It is said that the treaty was signed secretly, and it are still debated by scholars. → it is still debated (passive auxiliary must agree with the singular subject "it").

question:
Find the part of the sentence that contains an error. If the sentence is free from error, select 'No error'.

 

The company had the office renovate before the new financial year began (a)/ and also had all the computers upgraded (b)/ to improve overall efficiency. (c)/ No error (d)
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. (a).

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• In the causative construction "have something done", the object must be followed by the past participle: "had the office renovated", not the base form "renovate".

◦ Corrected sentence: The company had the office renovated before the new financial year began and also had all the computers upgraded to improve overall efficiency.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Part (b) is correct — "and also had all the computers upgraded" is a correctly formed causative construction.

 

• Part (c) is correct — "to improve overall efficiency" correctly completes the sentence.

 

• Option (d) No error — this is incorrect since an error exists in part (a).

 

NOTE

 

• She had her car repair at the local garage. → had her car repaired (causative "have + object + past participle").

question:
Find the part of the sentence that contains an error.

 

During the burglary last night, (a)/ the wooden door was broken by a heavy hammer left at the scene, (b)/ and the intruder was later identified (c)/ through the security camera footage. (d)
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. (b).

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• When the passive sentence refers to the instrument used to perform an action rather than the doer, the preposition "with" is used, not "by": "broken with a heavy hammer".

◦ Corrected sentence: During the burglary last night, the wooden door was broken with a heavy hammer left at the scene, and the intruder was later identified through the security camera footage.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Part (a) is correct — "During the burglary last night," is a proper introductory phrase.

 

• Part (c) is correct — "and the intruder was later identified" is a correctly formed passive.

 

• Part (d) is correct — "through the security camera footage" correctly completes the sentence.

 

NOTE

 

• The letter was written by a blue pen. → was written with a blue pen ("with" for the instrument, "by" for the doer of the action).

question:
Find the part of the sentence that contains an error.

 

The committee consists of seven members from different departments, (a)/ and its recommendations are consisted of detailed budget projections (b)/ that will guide the next fiscal year's spending, (c)/ pending final approval from the board. (d)
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. (b).

• The phrase "consist of" is a stative expression and therefore has no passive form; it must always be used in the active voice: "recommendations consist of...".

◦ Corrected sentence: The committee consists of seven members from different departments, and its recommendations consist of detailed budget projections that will guide the next fiscal year's spending, pending final approval from the board.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Part (a) is correct — "The committee consists of seven members from different departments," is correctly used in the active voice.

 

• Part (c) is correct — "that will guide the next fiscal year's spending," correctly completes the clause.

 

• Part (d) is correct — "pending final approval from the board" correctly completes the sentence.

 

NOTE

 

• The package is consisted of three separate components. → the package consists of three separate components ("consist of" is never used in the passive voice).

question:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

 

Given the missing files discovered this morning, the office safe ___ overnight, though the alarm never sounded.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. must have been broken into.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• With the modal perfect "must have been", the passive form of the phrasal verb "break into" is "must have been broken into", expressing a strong deduction about a completed past action.

◦ Complete sentence: Given the missing files discovered this morning, the office safe must have been broken into overnight, though the alarm never sounded.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 2: "must break into" — this drops the perfect aspect required to express a deduction about a completed past action.

 

• Option 3: "must have been breaking into" — the continuous form is wrongly used instead of the simple modal perfect passive "must have been broken into".

 

• Option 4: "must have broken into" — this is the active form; the passive auxiliary "been" is missing.

 

NOTE

 

• The vault must have been tampered with during the power outage. (modal perfect passive expressing a strong deduction about a completed past action).
